### Chapter 27: Decision-Aware Forecasting {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: sol-27-setup
#| include: false
source("R/_common.R")
library(tidypm)
R  <- as_xts_pm(sim_class_returns_monthly, date, class, return)
rf <- sim_riskfree_monthly$return
Re <- R - rf
N <- ncol(Re); Tn <- nrow(Re); dates <- zoo::index(R)
rf_by_month <- setNames(rf, as.character(dates))
mu <- colMeans(Re); S <- stats::cov(Re)
gamma <- 5
oos <- seq.int(121L, Tn)

# The chapter's helpers, repeated so that this fragment runs on its own.
correct_mean <- function(R, target = c("grand", "zero"), c = NULL) {
  target <- match.arg(target)
  X <- zoo::coredata(R); T <- nrow(X); N <- ncol(X)
  mu <- colMeans(X); S <- stats::cov(X)
  r   <- if (target == "grand") 1L else 0L
  Pmu <- if (target == "grand") rep(mean(mu), N) else rep(0, N)
  d   <- mu - Pmu
  q   <- as.numeric(t(d) %*% solve(S, d))
  if (is.null(c)) c <- (N - r - 2) * (T - 1) / (T - N + 2)
  h   <- max(1 - c / (T * q), 0)
  list(mu = setNames(Pmu + h * d, colnames(X)), factor = h, c = c, q = q, N = N, T = T)
}
gmv_qp <- function(S) {
  n <- ncol(S)
  sol <- quadprog::solve.QP(Dmat = 2 * S * 1e4, dvec = rep(0, n),
                            Amat = cbind(rep(1, n), diag(n)), bvec = c(1, rep(0, n)), meq = 1)
  w <- pmax(sol$solution, 0)
  setNames(w / sum(w), colnames(S))
}
tan_qp <- function(mu, S) {
  n <- length(mu)
  if (max(mu) <= 0) return(structure(gmv_qp(S), fallback = TRUE))
  sol <- quadprog::solve.QP(Dmat = 2 * S * 1e4, dvec = rep(0, n),
                            Amat = cbind(mu * 1e2, diag(n)), bvec = c(1, rep(0, n)), meq = 1)
  y <- pmax(sol$solution, 0)
  structure(setNames(y / sum(y), names(mu)), fallback = FALSE)
}
sharpe_realized <- function(r, rf) {
  n <- length(r)
  (prod(1 + r)^(12 / n) - prod(1 + rf)^(12 / n)) / (stats::sd(r) * sqrt(12))
}
ce_annual <- function(e) 12 * mean(e) - gamma / 2 * 12 * stats::var(e)

# A rolling sixty-month tangency backtest on a supplied estimator of the mean.
roll_tangency <- function(mean_fun, win = 60L) {
  out <- t(vapply(oos, function(m) {
    X <- Re[(m - win):(m - 1L), ]; V <- stats::cov(zoo::coredata(X))
    est <- mean_fun(X)
    w <- tan_qp(est$mu, V); stopifnot(identical(names(w), colnames(Re)))
    c(total = sum(w * zoo::coredata(R)[m, ]), factor = est$factor)
  }, numeric(2)))
  list(sharpe = sharpe_realized(out[, "total"], rf_by_month[as.character(dates[oos])]),
       factor = out[, "factor"])
}
```

#### Exercise 1

With the zero target the corrected mean is a positive multiple of the sample
mean whenever the factor is positive, and the long-only tangency problem is
invariant to a positive rescaling of the mean, so the weights, and hence the
realized returns, coincide month by month. On windows where the factor is
zero the corrected mean is the zero vector, `tan_qp()` falls back to minimum
variance, and the two rules part company.

```{r}
#| label: sol-27-ex1
sample_rule <- roll_tangency(function(X) list(mu = colMeans(zoo::coredata(X)), factor = 1))
zero_rule   <- roll_tangency(function(X) correct_mean(X, "zero"))
same_month  <- zero_rule$factor > 0
# Where the factor is positive the two rules hold the same portfolio; recompute
# the sample rule on those months only and compare.
sub_sharpe <- function(fun) {
  r <- vapply(oos[same_month], function(m) {
    X <- Re[(m - 60L):(m - 1L), ]; V <- stats::cov(zoo::coredata(X))
    sum(tan_qp(fun(X)$mu, V) * zoo::coredata(R)[m, ])
  }, numeric(1))
  sharpe_realized(r, rf_by_month[as.character(dates[oos[same_month]])])
}
stopifnot(all.equal(sub_sharpe(function(X) list(mu = colMeans(zoo::coredata(X)))),
                    sub_sharpe(function(X) correct_mean(X, "zero"))))
c(months_factor_zero = sum(!same_month), share = mean(!same_month),
  sharpe_sample = sample_rule$sharpe, sharpe_zero_target = zero_rule$sharpe)
```

On the `r sum(same_month)` months with a positive factor the two rules earn
identical returns, which the assertion confirms. On the remaining
`r sum(!same_month)` months the zero-target rule holds minimum variance, and
over the full period its Sharpe ratio is
`r sprintf("%.3f", zero_rule$sharpe)` against
`r sprintf("%.3f", sample_rule$sharpe)` for the sample mean: the entire
difference comes from the months on which the correction gave up on the mean
altogether.

```{r}
#| label: sol-27-ex1b
unc <- t(vapply(oos, function(m) {
  X <- Re[(m - 60L):(m - 1L), ]; Xm <- zoo::coredata(X); V <- stats::cov(Xm)
  ms <- list(sample = colMeans(Xm), zero = correct_mean(X, "zero")$mu, grand = correct_mean(X, "grand")$mu)
  vapply(ms, function(mu_) sum(solve(V, mu_) / gamma * zoo::coredata(Re)[m, ]), numeric(1))
}, numeric(3)))
lev <- mean(vapply(oos, function(m) {
  Xm <- zoo::coredata(Re[(m - 60L):(m - 1L), ]); sum(solve(stats::cov(Xm), colMeans(Xm))) / gamma
}, numeric(1)))
ce_unc <- apply(unc, 2, ce_annual)
stopifnot(all(ce_unc < 0), ce_unc[["zero"]] > ce_unc[["sample"]], ce_unc[["grand"]] > ce_unc[["sample"]])
round(c(leverage_sample = lev, ce_unc), 3)
```

The unconstrained plug-in position on the sample mean levers the sixteen
classes `r sprintf("%.1f", lev)` times on average and earns a certainty
equivalent of `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * ce_unc[["sample"]])` a year, worse
than the bill by a wide margin, as @eq-08-kz predicts for $T = 60$ and
$N = 16$. Both corrections cut the loss, to
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * ce_unc[["zero"]])` with the zero target and
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * ce_unc[["grand"]])` with the grand mean, and
neither reaches zero: the correction lowers the certainty-equivalent loss, as
@eq-27-risk says, and leaves the covariance channel of @eq-08-kz, the Wishart
factors that make the position so long, untouched.

#### Exercise 2

```{r}
#| label: sol-27-ex2
set.seed(1602)
L <- chol(S); Tm <- 60L
c_f <- (N - 3) * (Tm - 1) / (Tm - N + 2)
cs  <- c(half = c_f / 2, c_f = c_f, one_and_half = 1.5 * c_f, two_and_half = 2.5 * c_f)
rafe2 <- function(m_hat) as.numeric(t(m_hat - mu) %*% solve(S, m_hat - mu))
mc <- vapply(seq_len(2000L), function(b) {
  X <- xts::xts(matrix(rnorm(Tm * N), Tm) %*% L + matrix(mu, Tm, N, byrow = TRUE),
                order.by = dates[seq_len(Tm)])
  colnames(X) <- colnames(Re)
  vapply(cs, function(cc) rafe2(correct_mean(X, c = cc)$mu), numeric(1))
}, numeric(4))
risk <- rowMeans(mc)
stopifnot(risk[["c_f"]] < N / Tm, risk[["half"]] < N / Tm, risk[["one_and_half"]] < N / Tm)
round(c(N_over_T = N / Tm, risk), 4)

backtest <- vapply(cs, function(cc) roll_tangency(function(X) correct_mean(X, c = cc))$sharpe, numeric(1))
round(backtest, 3)
```

The interval of @eq-27-constant is $(0, 2c_f)$, so the first three constants
lie inside it and the fourth outside. In the simulation the three inside beat
$N/T = `r sprintf("%.3f", N / Tm)`$ and the one at $2.5\,c_f$ gives
`r sprintf("%.3f", risk[["two_and_half"]])`,
`r if (risk[["two_and_half"]] > N / Tm) "above" else "still below"` the sample
mean's risk; the positive part is why a constant outside the interval
`r if (risk[["two_and_half"]] > N / Tm) "still does not do much worse than the theorem's unclamped version would" else "does not do the damage the unclamped formula predicts"`,
because once $c/(T\hat{q})$ exceeds one the factor is held at zero rather
than turning negative. In the backtest the Sharpe ratio of the tangency rule
`r if (all(diff(backtest) >= 0)) "rises monotonically" else "does not move monotonically"`
with $c$, from `r sprintf("%.3f", backtest[["half"]])` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", backtest[["two_and_half"]])`: a larger constant shrinks
harder, more windows collapse onto minimum variance, and on this market
minimum variance is the better rule, so the Sharpe ratio rewards shrinkage
beyond the risk-minimizing constant. The two criteria disagree because the
theorem minimizes the risk of the mean while the backtest scores a long-only
rule against a rival that uses no mean.

#### Exercise 3

```{r}
#| label: sol-27-ex3
cv <- sim_curve_weekly |>
  dplyr::filter(series == "US_Slope") |> dplyr::arrange(date)
i_last <- findInterval(dates, cv$date)
term_lag <- xts::lag.xts(xts::xts(-cv$value[i_last], order.by = dates), 1)
F_term <- vapply(colnames(Re), function(s) {
  y <- as.numeric(Re[, s]); x <- as.numeric(term_lag)
  vapply(oos, function(m) {
    tr <- which(!is.na(x) & seq_len(Tn) < m)
    b <- stats::lm.fit(cbind(1, x[tr]), y[tr])$coefficients
    unname(b[1] + b[2] * x[m])
  }, numeric(1))
}, numeric(length(oos)))
dimnames(F_term) <- list(as.character(dates[oos]), colnames(Re))
vol60 <- zoo::rollapply(Re, 60, stats::sd, align = "right", fill = NA)
cost_rate <- pm_costs_default()[sub(".*_", "", colnames(Re))]; names(cost_rate) <- colnames(Re)
w_policy <- setNames(rep(1 / N, N), colnames(Re))

run_cells <- function(band) {
  kappa <- band / (0.5 / sqrt(12))
  tilt_from <- function(reduce) {
    W <- t(vapply(seq_along(oos), function(i) {
      m <- oos[i]; s <- F_term[i, ] / as.numeric(vol60[m - 1L, ]); s <- reduce(s - mean(s))
      tl <- pmin(pmax(kappa * s, -band), band)
      w <- w_policy + tl - mean(tl); w <- pmax(w, 0); w / sum(w)
    }, numeric(N)))
    dimnames(W) <- list(as.character(dates[oos]), colnames(Re)); W
  }
  steps3 <- function(s) stats::ave(s, ceiling(rank(s, ties.method = "first") * 3 / N))
  sign_only <- function(s) { g <- ceiling(rank(s, ties.method = "first") * 3 / N)
    (band / kappa) * (as.numeric(g == 3L) - as.numeric(g == 1L)) }
  cells <- list(every_magnitude = tilt_from(identity), three_groups = tilt_from(steps3),
                sign_only = tilt_from(sign_only), equal_weight = tilt_from(function(s) s * 0))
  t(vapply(cells, function(W) {
    Rm <- zoo::coredata(R)[oos, ]; Em <- zoo::coredata(Re)[oos, ]
    r <- rowSums(W * Rm); e <- rowSums(W * Em)
    drifted <- W * (1 + Rm) / (1 + r)
    trade <- abs(W[-1, ] - drifted[-nrow(W), ]); cost <- c(as.numeric(trade %*% cost_rate), 0)
    c(sharpe = sharpe_realized(r, rf_by_month[as.character(dates[oos])]),
      ce_net = ce_annual(e - cost), turnover = 12 * mean(c(rowSums(trade) / 2, 0)))
  }, numeric(3)))
}
narrow <- run_cells(0.5 / N); wide <- run_cells(1 / N)
spread <- function(x) diff(range(x[c("every_magnitude", "three_groups", "sign_only"), "sharpe"]))
round(cbind(narrow, wide), 4)
c(spread_narrow = spread(narrow), spread_wide = spread(wide))
```

Doubling the band roughly doubles every tilt, and the gain over equal
weighting grows with it, but the spread across the three forecast cells goes
from `r sprintf("%.3f", spread(narrow))` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", spread(wide))` in Sharpe ratio, which
`r if (spread(wide) > 2 * spread(narrow)) "is a visible widening" else "is still inside the noise of a single Sharpe ratio"`.
The sign cell `r if (wide["sign_only", "ce_net"] >= wide["every_magnitude", "ce_net"] - 5e-4) "still matches" else "now falls short of"`
the full vector after costs at the wider band, with turnover of
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * wide["sign_only", "turnover"])` against
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * wide["every_magnitude", "turnover"])`. What the
exercise shows is that the value of the term spread on these sixteen series
is set by how far the forecast is allowed to move the weights, the length of
the position in the language of @sec-27-decision-aware-forecasting-theory,
far more than by how finely its cross-section is resolved.

#### Exercise 4

```{r}
#| label: sol-27-ex4
V60 <- zoo::coredata(vol60)[oos - 1L, ]; Y <- zoo::coredata(Re)[oos, ]
ic_month <- vapply(seq_along(oos), function(i)
  stats::cor(F_term[i, ] / V60[i, ], Y[i, ] / V60[i, ], method = "spearman"), numeric(1))
# From the second out-of-sample year on, the trailing mean of the realized
# monthly coefficients over the months already forecast.
ic_trail <- c(rep(NA_real_, 12L), vapply(13:length(oos), function(i) mean(ic_month[seq_len(i - 1L)]), numeric(1)))
G_trail  <- (2 * N * (seq_along(oos) - 1L) * pmax(ic_trail, 0)^2 / (1 - pmax(ic_trail, 0)^2))^(1 / 3)
G_trail  <- pmax(1L, pmin(N %/% 2L, as.integer(round(G_trail))))
table(G_trail[-(1:12)])
c(share_one_group = mean(G_trail[-(1:12)] == 1L), mean_trailing_ic = mean(ic_trail, na.rm = TRUE))
```

Measured on the forecasts actually made, the trailing information coefficient
averages `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(ic_trail, na.rm = TRUE))`, and the rule
holds $1/N$, one group, in
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(G_trail[-(1:12)] == 1L))` of the months from
the second out-of-sample year on, with the rest at
`r paste(sort(unique(G_trail[-(1:12)][G_trail[-(1:12)] > 1L])), collapse = " or ")`
groups. The number read from fitted values in the chapter never fell below
three. A rule that chooses its granularity from the data is only as good as
the number it reads, and an in-sample fit overstates ranking ability for the
same reason an in-sample $R^2$ overstates predictability in
@sec-16-signals-and-forecasts-theory.
